content: Liar Game begins with 5 players and exactly one Liar. There will be 1 clue round(s), followed by one private vote from each player for another player. If the group accuses a non-liar, the Liar wins. If it accuses the Liar, the Liar gets one final word guess and still wins if correct; otherwise the non-liars win. Non-liars must both identify the Liar and keep the word difficult to guess. All clues are public. Malformed or self-votes abstain; ties accuse the earliest tied player in the configured player order.
Topic: Places.

You are a non-liar. The secret word is Church. Keep it secret from the Liar. The other non-liars already know it, so there is no need to teach them its definition or identifying features. Choose the form and point of view freely, and give one short clue connected to the word. Do not explicitly say the secret word.
You are the Liar. You do not know the secret word. Infer it from others' clues while blending in. Give a plausible clue on your turn.
Clue round 1/1. Public speaking order: Player 1, Player 2, Player 3, Player 4, Player 5.

Round 1/1: Player 1, You were not given the word. Use only the public clues so far to give a plausible indirect clue while concealing that uncertainty. If no clues have been spoken yet, use only the topic if it was revealed. Do not simply copy another player's clue verbatim. Your clue is PUBLIC. A word, short phrase, metaphor, or situational description is allowed; any point of view is allowed. Output one short clue only; do not name the secret word or declare your role.
